note: Every entry points at the vendor's own download. Windoz never ships Microsoft's binaries. A sha256 pin is verified exactly and a mismatch is refused (stale file). An entry without a pin freezes the first download's SHA-256 per prefix and refuses any later change unless the user accepts it explicitly.

components.title: Wine Mono (.NET Framework)
components.detail: Games built on Microsoft's .NET Framework run on Wine Mono, the Wine project's open-source runtime. Windoz downloads it from WineHQ and the engine links it into the prefix before each session.
components.note: Pinned to WineHQ's Wine Mono 11.0.0 and its SHA-256, exactly as Madeira's build pins it. About 42 MB to download, about 130 MB once installed.

components.title: Visual C++ 2005 runtime (VC80)
components.detail: Loads automatically for 64-bit games that import msvcr80/msvcp80.
components.note: Provided by the engine: Wine's built-in VC80 runtime, and the engine seeds the side-by-side assemblies into a new prefix, so games with activation contexts find it. Nothing to install.

components.title: Visual C++ 2008 runtime (VC90)
components.detail: Loads automatically for 64-bit games that import msvcr90/msvcp90.
components.note: Provided by the engine: Wine's built-in VC90 runtime, with side-by-side seeding like VC80. Nothing to install.

components.title: Visual C++ 2010 runtime (VC100)
components.detail: Loads automatically for 64-bit games that import msvcr100/msvcp100.
components.note: Provided by the engine: msvcr100/msvcp100 are Wine built-ins; 64-bit games load them without any install.

components.title: Visual C++ 2012 runtime (VC110)
components.detail: Loads automatically for 64-bit games that import msvcr110/msvcp110.
components.note: Provided by the engine: msvcr110/msvcp110 are Wine built-ins; 64-bit games load them without any install.

components.title: Visual C++ 2013 runtime (VC120)
components.detail: Loads automatically for 64-bit games that import msvcr120/msvcp120.
components.note: Provided by the engine: msvcr120/msvcp120 are Wine built-ins; 64-bit games load them without any install.

components.title: Visual C++ 2015–2022 runtime
components.detail: The runtime most modern games need (vcruntime140 / msvcp140 / concrt140 and friends).
components.note: Provided by the engine: every session overlays Microsoft's own x86-64 runtime DLLs, taken from the pinned, hash-checked vc-runtime-inputs copy the build already carries. The first session writes them into the prefix; until then this row says "staged at session start".

components.title: 32-bit (x86) runtimes — VC++ 2005–2022, DirectX setup, .NET installers
components.note: Not available in this build: the engine is 64-bit only (no 32-bit support yet), so 32-bit programs cannot start and their installers cannot run. Games that ship both builds work through their 64-bit executable; pick that one when adding the game.

components.title: Microsoft .NET Framework 4.8 (optional)
components.note: Not needed and not installable here: .NET Framework games run on Wine Mono (above). Microsoft's installer is a 32-bit bootstrapper that starts helper processes; this build can do neither.

components.title: .NET Desktop Runtime 8 (LTS)
components.detail: Only for games built against .NET 5 or newer (rare; most Unity and .NET Framework titles need Wine Mono instead).
components.note: No fixed hash: Microsoft's link follows the 8.0 servicing channel. Windoz records the exact file it first downloaded (SHA-256 and final URL) and refuses any later change unless you accept it. Microsoft's installer starts helper processes; if this session cannot finish it, Windoz reports the installer's own failure instead of pretending.

components.title: DirectX June 2010 redist (legacy D3DX)
components.detail: The last all-in-one DirectX package, for very old games that use the D3DX helper libraries.
components.note: Not installable in this build: Microsoft's package is a 32-bit self-extracting setup (DXSETUP) and cannot run without 32-bit support. The engine's built-in D3DX / D3D compiler libraries cover most games that ask for it.

components.title: Steam client components
components.detail: The Steam client files Valve's own client needs when Windoz starts a Steam game in Doz Dock.
components.note: Handled by the Steam sign-in flow: Windoz downloads Steam's components (about 72 MB from Valve's own CDN) as part of preparing a dock session — see the game's Steam card.

components.title: Game one-time installers (_CommonRedist)
components.detail: The redistributables a game ships in its own folder.
components.note: Listed per game: Windoz scans each game's folder (and Steam's shared redist folder) and shows the installers it finds on the game's page, with a Run button that starts them in a Windows session.
